subject: Addins and gadgets in a package, Imports vs Suggests

messages.author: 9a0033d9324fcea3
messages.subject: Addins and gadgets in a package, Imports vs Suggests
parts:
Context: an addin that enhances a package but that is "nice to have", not mission critical.

I've been reading here:

https://rstudio.github.io/rstudioaddins/#developing-addins
https://rstudio.github.io/rstudioaddins/#installation15

The official recommendation is to list rstudioapi under Imports and, if the addin is a gadget, ditto for Shiny and miniUI.

It seems like it would be better to Suggest these packages and then use `requireNamespace("foo", quietly = TRUE)` at the start of the addin.

But I don't have a lot of experience with Shiny or "Shiny in a package". Am I missing some reason to have a strong preference for Imports over Suggests in this context?

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Addins and gadgets in a package, Imports vs Suggests
parts:
If the addin is not a critical part of your package, I'd just use
Suggests instead of Imports. That is exactly what I did for bookdown:
https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/master/DESCRIPTION If shiny
and miniUI are missing when a user clicks the addin, I think there
will be a warning dialog in the RStudio IDE to ask the user to install
them.

Regards,
Yihui
